signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Data Divergence
signals.text: CAD/JPY is the dominant bilateral theme as CAD averages +0.691% outperformance across its G10 peers while JPY lags at -0.765% (1.456% spread). The CAD outperformance is supported by a moderate positive ESI of +12.0, contrasting with JPY’s recentfutures decline following trade deficit data. The 125bp CORRA-TONA OIS carry differential structurally favors CAD, and the pair currently benefits from crude oil's three-session rally to $83.7. JPY remains under broad pressure despite bond yields rising on hike expectations, as carry-trade dominance persists while VIX remains at 15.4. Trade bias: Long CAD/JPY; strong CAD data and carry advantage favor continued divergence. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: WTI oil reversal below $80/bbl or a VIX spike above 25 triggers a JPY safe-haven bid.

signals.title: AUD/USD — RBA Hawkishness vs Positioning + Retail
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7056, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6928–0.7009). RBA Governor Bullock's recent comments maintain a hawkish stance, noting that rate hikes remain 'front of mind' despite the board's decision to wait for more information. This hawkishness conflicts with a crowded speculative long (COT LF net +37,990, 72.1% long) and an extreme retail short (78% short), creating a high-conviction divergence setup. While the -73bp OIS carry premium favors AUD, the positioning concentration suggests limited upside without a fresh fundamental driver. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; RBA hawkishness supports the bid against retail fading. Catalyst: US CPI this week. Risk: RBA pivot to neutral or a break below the SMA20 at 0.7009.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY at 159.29 trades below its SMA20/50 cluster (161.08/161.16) but above the SMA200 at 158.09. The 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential remains the primary driver, yet the options market shows a strong -2.18 25d RR put skew, signaling heavy demand for downside protection. This divergence between carry-positive spot and defensive options positioning highlights a lack of conviction in the current USD bid. Furthermore, JPY's correlation with VIX has turned positive (z=+1.48σ), suggesting the yen is no longer acting as a traditional safe-haven during minor equity fluctuations. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; carry support is offset by defensive options positioning. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 49% hike priced) 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 raises BoJ intervention risk.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Risk Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3497 is consolidating above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3367–1.3420). The options market is pricing a massive 5.0% Volatility Risk Premium, with 11.0% IV significantly outstripping 6.0% realized vol (HV30). This elevated premium suggests traders are paying for protection ahead of the UK GDP and US CPI releases, despite neutral speculative positioning (COT LF net +39,039). The SOFR-SONIA OIS spread is near neutral at -11bp, removing the carry component as a directional driver for now. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; elevated IV premium makes new long positions expensive. Catalyst: UK GDP release this week. Risk: Break below the SMA200 at 1.3408 invalidates the bullish technical structure.
